steps.prompt: Two triangles share the same base, and their top corners lie on a line parallel to that base. Which one has the larger area?

cards.title: Half base times height
cards.body: The area of a triangle is $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$, where the height is perpendicular to the base (it may fall outside the triangle). Heron's formula needs only the sides: with $s = \frac{a + b + c}{2}$, the area is $\sqrt{s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)}$.

cards.title: Worked example: Heron
cards.problem: A triangle has sides $13$, $14$ and $15$. What is its area?

cards.title: Area tricks
cards.body: Triangles with the same height have areas in the same ratio as their bases, so a median cuts a triangle into two equal halves. For awkward shapes, split into pieces, or surround the shape with a rectangle and subtract the corners.

cards.title: Worked example: splitting a base
cards.problem: Triangle $ABC$ has area $30$. $D$ is on $BC$ with $BD : DC = 2 : 3$. What is the area of triangle $ABD$?

steps.text: $ABD$ and $ABC$ share the height from $A$, and $BD$ is $\frac{2}{5}$ of $BC$.

cards.title: The common trap: a slanted side as the height
cards.body: The height must meet the base at a right angle; a slanted side is not the height. In Heron's formula, $s$ is HALF the perimeter. And don't forget the $\frac{1}{2}$.
